coverage_note: A reviewed core library of vanilla recipes and construction paths. Community-server mods can change recipes, and are deliberately kept separate until their exact mod documentation is supplied.

recipes.name: Rope from rags
steps: Combine two full stacks of six rags.
recipes.notes: Rope is used in many kits, fishing and improvised bags.

recipes.name: Rope from guts
steps: Combine the guts with a sharp tool.
recipes.notes: Wash hands after handling raw animal materials.

recipes.name: Splint
steps: Combine one of the listed bindings with two short sticks.
recipes.notes: Use to treat a broken leg.

recipes.name: Simple fishing rod
steps: Combine the long stick with rope.
Attach a fishing hook and bait before fishing.
recipes.notes: A basic sustainable-food setup once paired with a hook and bait.

recipes.name: Bone fishing hook
steps: Combine bones with a sharp tool.
recipes.notes: Attach it to a simple fishing rod, then add bait.

recipes.name: Wooden fishing hooks
steps: Combine a short stick with a sharp tool.
recipes.notes: A quick alternative when bones are unavailable.

recipes.name: Small fish trap
steps: Combine a plastic bottle with a sharp tool, then deploy the trap in suitable water.
recipes.notes: Check it later rather than expecting an instant catch.

recipes.name: Fish net trap
steps: Combine metal wire and netting, then deploy the trap in suitable water.
recipes.notes: A larger passive fishing option.

recipes.name: Tripwire
steps: Combine the wire and sticks, then place the completed tripwire.
recipes.notes: The placed tripwire can be configured with compatible attachments.

recipes.name: Rabbit snare
steps: Combine the wire and short stick, then place the snare in an appropriate area.
recipes.notes: It is a passive trap, so return later to check it.

recipes.name: Short sticks from a long stick
steps: Combine a long stick with a sharp tool.
recipes.notes: Short sticks are used in splints, kits, fires and traps.

recipes.name: Short sticks from firewood
steps: Combine firewood with a hatchet or axe.
recipes.notes: Useful when you have already prepared firewood.

recipes.name: Wooden planks from a log
steps: Combine a wooden log with a hacksaw.
recipes.notes: Planks are used by fences, crates and other base construction.

recipes.name: Burlap strips
steps: Combine a burlap sack with a sharp tool.
recipes.notes: Used for improvised bags and ghillie pieces.

recipes.name: Metal wire from barbed wire
steps: Combine barbed wire with pliers.
recipes.notes: Used in traps and flag-pole construction.

recipes.name: Wooden crate
steps: Combine the planks and nails while using a hammer or hatchet.
recipes.notes: A compact crafted storage container.

recipes.name: Improvised courier bag
steps: Combine a burlap sack and rope.
recipes.notes: Upgrade it with three short sticks for an improvised backpack.

recipes.name: Improvised backpack
steps: Combine an improvised courier bag with three short sticks.
recipes.notes: Craft the courier bag first if you do not already have one.

recipes.name: Fireplace
steps: Combine a short stick with one suitable kindling material.
Add fuel and use a compatible ignition source to light it.
recipes.notes: The placed fireplace can be upgraded with stones or a cooking stand.

recipes.name: Stone circle fireplace
steps: Add eight large stones to a placed fireplace.
recipes.notes: A placed construction upgrade, not a loose inventory combination.

recipes.name: Stone oven
steps: Add sixteen large stones to a placed fireplace.
recipes.notes: A placed construction upgrade, not a loose inventory combination.

recipes.name: Cooking stand
steps: Combine the sticks, then attach the stand to a suitable fireplace.
recipes.notes: The stand is a fireplace attachment.

recipes.name: Fire barrel
steps: Combine the barrel with a sharp tool.
recipes.notes: Prepare it safely before adding fuel and lighting it.

recipes.name: Improvised torch
steps: Combine a short stick with rags.
recipes.notes: Light it only when ready; it reveals your position at night.

recipes.name: Fence kit
steps: Combine two short sticks and rope.
Place the kit in its final orientation before beginning construction.
recipes.notes: The kit is the starting point for a vanilla fence or gate.

recipes.name: Fence base
steps: Place a fence kit.
Add two logs and build the base with a digging tool.
recipes.notes: Build a base first; wall frames are constructed on the placed base.

recipes.name: Fence frame stages
steps: Build the lower frame with 4 planks and 8 nails.
Build the upper frame with 5 planks and 10 nails.
recipes.notes: This total covers both frame stages only. Add the wall sections separately when you want the fence enclosed.

recipes.name: Wooden fence wall section
steps: Build either the lower or upper wooden wall on an already framed fence.
recipes.notes: Repeat this recipe for each wooden wall section you want on the framed fence.

recipes.name: Metal fence panel
steps: Build the chosen lower or upper metal wall section on a framed fence.
recipes.notes: These materials are for one metal wall section; build the fence base and frame first.

recipes.name: Watchtower kit
steps: Combine four short sticks and rope.
Place the kit before adding logs, planks, nails and the correct construction tools.
recipes.notes: Construction materials depend on the levels and sections you build.

recipes.name: Shelter kit
steps: Combine four short sticks and rope.
Place the kit before supplying the materials for a shelter variant.
recipes.notes: Choose improvised, tarp or leather shelter after the kit is placed.

recipes.name: Improvised shelter
steps: Place a shelter kit.
Add four long sticks and fifty short sticks, then finish the available construction actions.
recipes.notes: The most material-heavy but fully improvised shelter path.

recipes.name: Tarp shelter
steps: Place a shelter kit.
Add four long sticks and four tarps, then finish the available construction actions.
recipes.notes: A lower-stick alternative to the improvised shelter.

recipes.name: Leather shelter
steps: Place a shelter kit.
Add four long sticks and eight tanned leather pieces, then finish the available construction actions.
recipes.notes: Use vanilla tanned leather; modded leather items are separate.

recipes.name: Flag Pole Kit
steps: Combine three short sticks and rope.
Place the kit where the flag pole will stand.
recipes.notes: This is the start of a full Flag Pole, not a complete territory flag by itself.

recipes.name: Flag Pole construction
steps: Build the base with 1 log and a sledgehammer.
Build the support with 32 large stones and 6 more logs using a shovel or pickaxe.
Build the pole with 3 logs, 60 nails, rope and metal wire using a hammer or hatchet.
Attach and raise a flag to activate the territory-lifetime refresh.
recipes.notes: A raised flag pole refreshes supported object lifetimes in its vanilla 60-metre area; the flag needs periodic raising.

recipes.name: Improvised bolt
steps: Combine a short stick with a sharp tool.
recipes.notes: Can be upgraded with feathers.

recipes.name: Feathered bolt
steps: Combine an improvised bolt and feathers.
recipes.notes: Use the correct compatible crossbow.

recipes.name: Improvised bottle suppressor
steps: Combine a plastic bottle and duct tape.
Attach only to a compatible firearm.
recipes.notes: Improvised suppressors wear out quickly.
